findings.title: website_name leaks the website field for TL0 users viewed anonymously, bypassing untrusted_attributes
findings.body: The serializer deliberately hides `:website` (via `untrusted_attributes`, which checks `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`) so that anonymous visitors cannot see a TL0 user's profile fields. The new `:website_name` attribute is declared in the plain `attributes` list (line 43), is derived directly from `object.user_profile.website`, and its inclusion check only tests `website.present?` — it never checks `restrict_user_fields?`. As a result, for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor, `website` is omitted from the JSON but `website_name` (containing the website host, and possibly path) is still serialized, leaking exactly the information the restriction is meant to hide. The existing 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' spec was not extended to cover `website_name`, so the test suite does not catch this. `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes` or its include check should mirror `include_website?`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' suffix, so ActiveModelSerializers never calls it
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers filters attributes by calling `include_<attribute>?` (with a question mark) — every other filter in this file follows that convention (`include_email?`, `include_stats?`, etc.). The new method is defined as `def include_website_name` without the `?`, making it dead code: the `website.present?` guard never runs, and `website_name` is always serialized (as `nil` when the user has no website, and unconditionally in the restricted-TL0 case described above). Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Sibling subdomains are treated as the same domain as the instance
findings.body: The middle branch compares hosts of equal label count by stripping the first label from both sides: `www.anything.com` vs `forum.anything.com` are considered 'the same domain' and the full URL path is displayed. A sibling subdomain is not the instance's domain — on multi-tenant or shared-domain setups (e.g. instance at `forum.example.com`, user website at `evil.example.com/phishing-page`) the profile will render the full path as if the link belonged to the site's own domain, which is exactly the misleading display this feature is supposed to avoid. The comparison should only show the path when the website host equals the instance host or is a parent domain of it (the first and third branches), not when it is merely a sibling.
